body: The battle for control of Congress is beginning to take shape, and one question is dominating voter searches ahead of the 2026 elections: Who is winning the midterms right now?

While Election Day is still months away, new polling, primary results and election forecasts are offering some of the clearest signals yet about which party may emerge with the upper hand in Washington.

Republicans currently control the White House, both chambers of Congress, the gubernatorial majority and hold a conservative majority on the Supreme Court. However, the midterms in November can change that with 435 House seats up for election, 35 Senate seats and dozens of governor races on the ballot across the country.

Control of the House and Senate after the 2026 midterm elections will determine whether President Donald Trump can continue advancing his agenda with support from Congress or whether Democrats can regain enough seats to block, reshape or challenge key administration priorities...including another possible impeachment.
Here's how the race for control of the House and Senate look now and what the 2026 midterm election predictions and odds show.
